title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a programmatic research agenda, not a worked argument. Its title is 'Foncteurs fibres motiviques, et groupes fondamentaux motiviques' (motivic fibre functors and motivic fundamental groups). It is a list of topics 'à examiner' (to examine), some marked 'OK' or '*'. In modern language the programme reads as follows.

(0) 'VA à la Weil', with the interlinear addition 'Conditions de Hodge–Riemann'. This refers to abelian varieties built à la Weil, i.e. Weil's intermediate Jacobian. Weil's choice of complex structure makes the Hodge–Riemann bilinear relations give a polarization, so the result is always an abelian variety. The idea is that this should lead to (realize) pure motives of odd weight. In other words, odd-weight pure motives should be controlled by abelian varieties via Weil-type Jacobians.

(1) Marked OK and *. 'Extension du groupe [de Galois?] par des pro-[motiviques/algébriques]', with 'Groupe fondamental motivique' underlined below. This is the motivic analogue of the fundamental exact sequence 1 → π1(X_k̄) → π1(X) → Gal(k̄/k) → 1. The motivic π1 of X, defined Tannakianly from motives over X with a fibre functor at a point, should be an extension of the motivic Galois group of k by a pro-algebraic geometric part.

(2) Relations with class field theory, presumably the abelianized motivic π1 against the class-field-theoretic description of abelian π1.

(3) Marked OK. The case of Spec of a finite field, with the question whether partial motivic fibre functors with values in R exist ('???'). This is the known obstruction. For a supersingular elliptic curve E over F_q, End⁰(E) is the quaternion algebra ramified at p and ∞. So E ⊗ R is the Hamilton quaternions, which is not split, and the category of motives over F_q admits no Q-, R- or Q_p-valued fibre functor. Grothendieck is asking whether partial fibre functors survive.

(4) Marked *. The role of the motivic fundamental group for understanding algebraic cycles (reading uncertain), with two sub-cases. In the Hodge-conjecture case: Hodge classes versus 'transcendental' cycles, and two cycles differing by something. In the l-adic (Tate) case: transcendental classes. The implied principle is that algebraic classes should be the invariants of the motivic (Galois/fundamental) group, and that comparing motivic π1 with its Hodge (Mumford–Tate) and l-adic (monodromy/Galois image) realizations governs the Hodge and Tate conjectures. This includes variational/monodromy-invariance statements in families.

(5) Relations of (4) with older conjectures, probably the standard conjectures.

(6) L-functions and their functional equation.

(7) Marked OK. Positive structures, i.e. polarizations, later Saavedra's 'structures de polarisation' and the Hodge standard conjecture.

(8) 'Topologie à mettre sur Z', a topology to be put on Z. This is unclear; possibly coefficients, or Spec Z / arithmetic site.

(9) The Riemann hypothesis, with '??'.

The bottom note proposes proving Hodge-type positivity (the Hodge standard conjecture) by reducing to questions about divisors. The means would be blowing up, which turns a subvariety into an exceptional divisor, or (Picard/intermediate?) Jacobians. For divisors the Hodge index theorem is known in all characteristics. The overall aim is a Tannakian 'motivic Galois theory' covering the arithmetic of motives: class field theory, L-functions, the Riemann hypothesis, positivity, and algebraic cycles.
errors: No mathematical errors: the page is a list of questions. Item (3) is correctly flagged with '???'. Over F_q there is in fact no R-valued fibre functor on the full category of motives, because of supersingular elliptic curves. So any 'partial' fibre functor must be restricted to a subcategory, e.g. motives with commutative endomorphisms or ordinary objects.

The bottom suggestion (reducing Hodge positivity to divisors via blow-up) has an obvious gap. Blowing up a codimension-c cycle produces a divisor, but the intersection form on primitive classes of higher degree is not recovered from the divisor's Néron–Severi form alone. No such reduction is known to work in positive characteristic.

ideas.what: Motivic fundamental group of a variety as Tannakian group of motives over X with a fibre functor, sitting in an extension of the motivic Galois group of the base by a geometric pro-algebraic group
ideas.modern_name: Motivic fundamental group / motivic π1 exact sequence (relative Tannakian categories of motives, mixed motivic π1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'), with later work by Deligne–Goncharov, Ayoub, Nori
ideas.where_published: Motivic Galois group mentioned in Récoltes et Semailles; anabelian π1 in the letter to Faltings and the Esquisse d'un programme. An explicit 'groupe fondamental motivique' of a variety is not clearly in published texts.

ideas.what: Odd-weight pure motives realized through Weil-type (polarized) intermediate Jacobians, using the Hodge–Riemann conditions
ideas.modern_name: Weil intermediate Jacobian; motives of abelian type / algebraic representative (Murre)

ideas.what: Fibre functors on motives over a finite field: question of R-valued (partial) fibre functors
ideas.modern_name: Non-neutrality of motives over F_q; Weil-number / pseudomotivic groupoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (obstruction via supersingular curves), Saavedra, Deligne–Milne (1982), Langlands–Rapoport, Milne

ideas.what: Motivic π1 / motivic Galois group invariants governing algebraic cycles: Hodge conjecture vs Hodge classes, Tate conjecture vs l-adic classes
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian formulation of Hodge/Tate conjectures (Mumford–Tate group equals motivic Galois group); variational Hodge conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (variational Hodge conjecture, 1966 de Rham paper footnote), Deligne (absolute Hodge cycles, 1982), Serre (motivic Galois group conjectures), André
ideas.where_published: Variational Hodge conjecture: 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966)

ideas.modern_name: Polarized Tannakian categories; Hodge standard conjecture
ideas.where_published: 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (1969); Saavedra's thesis

ideas.what: Reduce Hodge-type positivity to divisors by blowing up or via Jacobians
ideas.modern_name: Strategy toward the Hodge standard conjecture in char p
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard attribution; the divisor/surface case is due to Segre and Grothendieck (1958)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly links a Tannakian 'motivic fundamental group' of a variety, as an extension of the Galois group, to the Hodge and Tate conjectures, class field theory, L-function functional equations and the Riemann hypothesis. This puts the motivic π1 inside the motive programme well before Deligne's 1989 introduction of motivic π1.
missed.quote: Foncteurs fibres motiviques, et groupes fondamentaux motiviques ... Rôle du groupe fondamental motivique pour la compréhension des [cycles?]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical priority and framing evidence. It suggests Grothendieck saw relative motivic π1 (not just the motivic Galois group of a field) as a tool for algebraic cycles, close to modern 'motivic monodromy' approaches to variational Hodge/Tate questions.

missed.claim: Proposal to prove Hodge-type positivity by reduction to divisors via blow-ups or Jacobians.
missed.quote: Positivité à la Hodge en se ramenant à des questions de diviseurs par éclatement, ou variétés de jacobiennes ??
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The Hodge standard conjecture in positive characteristic remains open beyond surfaces and a few cases (abelian fourfolds, Ancona). This records an unpursued, though likely insufficient, strategy.

missed.claim: Question of partial R-valued fibre functors on motives over a finite field.
missed.quote: Cas du spectre d'un corps fini. [Foncteurs?] motiviques partiels à valeurs dans R ???
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This anticipates the later analysis of non-neutral motives over F_q (Deligne–Milne, Langlands–Rapoport, Milne's Weil-number groupoids). It is now largely understood, so it is mainly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: It is known that Grothendieck envisaged a motivic Galois group. An explicit agenda titled 'motivic fibre functors and motivic fundamental groups' is less documented. It includes the motivic π1 as a Galois extension, applications to Hodge/Tate cycles, the R-valued fibre functor question over F_q, and a blow-up strategy for Hodge positivity. Still, it consists only of headings, and the ideas were all later developed by others.
transcription_corrections: Line 0: 'Conditions de Hodge-Riemann ...' is an interlinear insertion; 'VA à la Weil' is circled.

Line (1): 'Extension de groupe différentiel par des pluri-motiviques' is doubtful; more likely 'Extension du groupe [de Galois] par des pro-[algébriques/motiviques]', with 'Groupe fondamental motivique' underlined beneath.
Line (3): 'Pts motiviques partiels' may be '[Foncteurs fibres] motiviques partiels'; uncertain.

Item 4: 'schémas canoniques' is likely 'cycles algébriques'. 'Cas de Hodge' should be 'Conj. de Hodge' and 'Cas l-adique' should be 'Conj. l-adique'. The bracketed sub-entries read approximately '2 cycles ... par des plus diff[?] / cycles transcendants et cycles de Hodge' and '2 cycles transcendants'.
Item 5: 'avec un autre anciennes' is probably 'avec mes autres conjectures' or 'conjectures anciennes'; 'de 4)' is an interlinear insertion.
Bottom note: 'variétés de jacobiennes' is uncertain, possibly 'variétés jacobiennes' or 'de Picard'.
